## SECURITIES AND FUTURES COMMISSION

12th Floor, Edinburgh Tower, The Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong

## Circular to Registered Persons Regarding the Marketing of Hedge Funds (GC03/02 - 225/IP/6116)

The  Securities  and  Futures  Commission  notes  that  a  wide  range  of  collective  investment schemes  is  being  sold  in  the  retail  market.  Most  recently,  the  Commission  has  authorized public hedge funds. As a matter of principle, the Commission welcomes product innovation and the expansion of investment choices for investors. However, in view of the diversity and complexity of hedge funds and the inherent risks involved, the Commission wishes to remind registered persons that they should comply with the Code of Conduct for Persons Registered with the SFC and adopt fair dealing when marketing hedge funds to investors.

Hedge funds are a type of collective investment schemes. There is no universal definition of hedge funds.  They  vary  enormously  in  terms  of  their  investment  returns,  risk  profiles  and investment strategies. Although hedge funds are often marketed as 'all weather' funds that are able to perform under different market conditions, they are not 'sure-win' products. For some hedge funds, substantial loss of capital is possible. Investors should make sure that they fully understand the nature and risks involved before buying hedge funds.

Here are some key measures that registered persons are expected to observe with regards to the marketing of hedge funds except where these are waived under the Code of Conduct for Persons Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission:

1. Know Your Client: To ensure that hedge funds are suitable for their clients, registered persons should take all reasonable steps beforehand to obtain and verify the identity of the client  as  well  as  to  establish  the  financial  situation,  investment  experience,  investment objectives, time horizon and risk tolerance of the client. This will help registered persons to properly assess their client's ability to bear the financial risks and potential losses that may arise from investing in hedge funds.
2. Give Reasonable Advice: Registered persons should provide clear and reasonable advice to clients and ensure any representations made and information provided to the client are accurate and not misleading. When recommending hedge funds to their clients, registered persons  should  ensure  that  the  suitability  of  the  recommendation  for  those  clients  is reasonable in all the circumstances.
3. Fit and Proper Staff: The senior management of registered persons should ensure that their  employees  are  suitably  qualified  and  have  received  proper  training  to  a  level commensurate with their responsibilities in marketing hedge funds.

## Circular to Registered Persons Regarding the Marketing of Hedge Funds page 2

4. Information for Clients: Registered persons should provide their clients with pertinent information  regarding  the  hedge  funds.    These  include  the  provision  of  the  scheme prospectus  prior  to  subscription  by  the  client,  and  where  appropriate,  other  relevant scheme  information  that  would  assist  the  client  in  making  an  informed  investment decision.

The  Commission  strongly  urges  registered  persons  to  provide  clients  with  relevant, balanced  and  responsible  investor  education  materials  in  marketing  hedge  funds.  The Commission has issued education leaflets titled "How Much Do You Know About Hedge Funds" and "Ten Questions to Ask Before Investing in a Fund". Copies of the leaflets are available by calling Investor Education and Communications Department at 2842-7711. Other investor education information on hedge funds and traditional funds is available on the SFC-operated Electronic Investor Resources Centre at www.hkeirc.org .

5. Internal  Control  Procedures : Registered persons should set appropriate internal controls procedures with respect to the marketing of hedge  funds. Their senior management  assumes  full  responsibility  for  the  development,  implementation  and  ongoing effectiveness of the internal controls and the adherence thereto.

For more details, registered persons should refer to the Code of Conduct which is available on the Commission's website at www.hksfc.org.hk .
